findings.location: Approach / Scope — src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py ('parse the ticket description's ## Acceptance Criteria section')

Name this reuse in Scope so the close precheck and check-ac cannot drift on section boundaries.

findings.finding: The plan's blanket precheck ('any unchecked - [ ] fails the close deterministically before any LLM call') would fail-close on legitimately-unchecked `- [ ] [operator-attested] …` criteria, which ADR-0043 establishes are verified MET by the LLM completion verifier via a recorded attestation rather than by ticking the box — an existing in-repo convention the plan does not enumerate or exempt.
findings.location: Plan 'Approach' and AC line 2 ('Prose-only AC ... are unaffected'); interacts with docs/adr/0043-operator-attested-completion-evidence.md and the operator-attested matcher (det_operator_attested).
findings.suggested_fix: When scanning the AC block, treat a `- [ ]` line whose text begins (case-insensitively) with the `[operator-attested]` tag as NOT a completeness violation — defer it to the verifier — and state this exemption in the Approach/AC alongside the prose-only carve-out.

findings.finding: The plan blocks on ANY unchecked '- [ ]' with no exemption for [operator-attested] AC items, which by design have 'done' evidence outside the code snapshot/session and are legitimately left unchecked at close (satisfied by a recorded attestation comment).
findings.location: Approach / Testing — precheck fires on any '- [ ]'; Scope lists no operator-attested carve-out
findings.suggested_fix: When scanning AC lines, skip any line matching det_operator_attested._OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE so operator-attested criteria (whose evidence is recorded out-of-band) never trip the precheck.

findings.finding: The plan's 0-FP claim ('0/823 verifier-passed closes had unchecked boxes') is contradicted by an observed verifier-passed close that carried unchecked boxes (a8e5), so the backtest either measured a different signal than the mechanism checks or is unsound as the safety guarantee.
findings.location: Context / Problem — 'Backtest: 0/823 verifier-passed closes had unchecked boxes' and AC line 3

findings.finding: The precheck's decision rule ('any unchecked `- [ ]` AC item → deterministically fail the close before the LLM') never accounts for the established `[operator-attested]` AC-vocabulary value, whose done-evidence lives outside the codebase and whose checkbox is legitimately left unchecked — so the precheck would hard-block closing a class of tickets the completion verifier currently PASSES.
findings.location: Approach ('if any - [ ] checkbox remains unchecked, fail the close deterministically') + Acceptance Criteria lines 1 and 3
findings.suggested_fix: When scanning the AC block, skip `- [ ]` lines whose text (after the checkbox) begins with the exact case-insensitive `[operator-attested]` token, reusing det_operator_attested's canonical matcher rather than re-deriving it; only NON-operator-attested unchecked boxes trigger the deterministic block. Add a test asserting a ticket whose sole unchecked AC is `[operator-attested]` proceeds to the verifier.

findings.finding: The mechanism assumes an unchecked '- [ ]' AC item signals incompleteness, but the established close contract confirms completion via the LLM verifier reading the code, NOT via checkbox state — ACs are authored '- [ ]' and the closing agent does not check them. The precheck would produce false rejections and break existing passing behavior.
findings.location: Approach — 'if any - [ ] checkbox remains unchecked, fail the close deterministically'
